contract: The actual20-command system table resolves command0007 to r1_touch_switch_handler_plan_decode. The handler is ordinary C with one initialized private response word, replacing the assembly saved-register frame and separate kernel. Scratch and seed are unused in the C contract. Other advertised values preserve the native unsigned getter behavior on a readable backing buffer.

Selector1 logs the live switch byte and returns the native scalar logging-mode shift or SDK seam result; it does not change touch ownership. Selector2 logs, freshly rereads the live switch byte, and opens touch source0 for nonzero or closes source0 for zero. Repeated logging-mode reads preserve short-circuit order and scalar results.

The actual source module lookup/dispatcher/table, payload getter, checked-send/header wrappers and touch open/close/client owner execute in the replay. All existing touch clients and thread owners are reused.
limits: Logging, final protocol response service, RTOS flags and synthetic release are modeled. The response backend captures actual eight-byte headers and one-byte payloads, mutates the private acknowledgement byte and can mutate the incoming payload/client state at explicit backend boundaries. Physical transport, sensor state, RTOS concurrency and final firmware boot are not exercised.

Cases cover all256 selectors, all256 switch bytes, all logging branches, handle/advertised-length guards, live callback mutations and ownership masks. The normal C contract compares scalar results, emitted response headers/data, provider traces, public packet/client state, callee-saved integer/FP registers, masks, SP and stack/input guards. Native restored r1/r2/r3, private acknowledgement addresses and arbitrary external scratch-register consumers are excluded. Current source caller audit supports this boundary; no byte-identity or hybrid private-ABI guarantee is made.
